newsitem.title: USA: U.S.-U.K. aviation talks end without accord.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-U.K. aviation talks end without accord.

text.p: U.S. and British aviation negotiators ended three days of talks on Thursday without reaching an agreement on a free market aviation accord, a spokeswoman for the Transportation Department said.
The delegations agreed to continue discussing the matter through diplomatic channels and to consider scheduling another face-to-face meeting, spokeswoman Wendy Burt said.
"The delegations concurred that the talks had been useful and that they achieved a fuller understanding of their respective positions," Burt said.
The negotiators stopped short of scheduling another meeting. "They need to talk more before a further round is scheduled," Burt said.
A State Department official on Wednesday said he could not report on whether any progress was being made in the talks, which have been been held, on and off, for the past two years.

The United States wants to end the current restrictive U.S.-British aviation services agreement and replace it with an "open skies" pact that would give airlines greater freedom to fly routes and frequencies of their own choosing.
Past talks have been held up by Britain's reluctance to allow additional U.S. flights to London Heathrow airport, which is dominated by British Airways Plc..
Heathrow is considered a key transfer point for travel beyond Britain to continental Europe.
